none: The Kasner spacetime has no conformal diagram that tells its directions apart. Each plane of $t$ and one of $x$, $y$ and $z$ is totally geodesic, and on it the metric $-c^2dt^2 + t^{2p_i}dx_i^2$ is flat in the time $c\,t^{1 - p_i}/(1 - p_i)$, which runs from zero to infinity for every exponent below one. So all three planes give the same half of Minkowski's diamond, the singularity along its lower edge.
